To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dehydration propensity of a soluble protein is determined by a large cluster of packing defects, which are the promoters of protein associations and are the source of a local electrostatic enhancement.
large clusters of hydrogen bond defects are the most significant dehydration promoters on the surface of folded proteins, and that they induce strong local dielectric quenching.
the largest clusters of order-disorder packing defects in soluble proteins are associated with the most pronounced dehydration hotspots, which in turn induce the strongest electrostatic enhancement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural singularity of order-disorder regions in soluble proteins, and its role in the dehydration and electrostatics of protein surfaces.
the identification and analysis of structural features of order-disorder intermediates that are related to protein associations.
the structural and functional consequences of the dehydration propensity of order-disordered intermediate regions in soluble folded proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of large clusters of packing defect is a structural signature that identifies a class of proteins that are prone to dehydration, electrostatic enhancement and structural instability.

a large cluster of packing defects in the protein structure is a structural singularity with a strong dehydration propensity and a significant electrostatic modulation, which can be related to the functional properties of the protein.
the proteins with large packing defect clusters are prone to dehydration and to protein-protein interactions, and they may be involved in protein aggregation and in the onset of amyloidogenicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a large cluster of packing defects in soluble folded proteins is a structural singularity, which signals the protein's vulnerability, dehydration propensity, and electrostatic enhancement.
the presence of large clusters of packing defect is a hallmark of proteins that are prone to dehydration and electrostatic enhancement.
large clusters of order-disorder defects are the structural signature of proteins that are prone to aggregation, are highly interactive, and are involved in the regulation of cell signaling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
large clusters of order-disorder packing defects are the structural basis of protein associations and are the key to understanding protein interactions and their functional consequences.
a protein with a large concentration of packing defect clusters is a protein with a high propensity for association, aggregation and amyloid formation.
the dehydration propensity and the electrostatic enhancement of these packing defect clusters may have important implications for the understanding of the structural basis of protein associations.
